macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global stocks edge higher as markets await U.S. inflation data
items.summary: Global equities inched higher, with oil broadly steady as investors weighed Strait of Hormuz shipping developments and looked ahead to key U.S. inflation data due midweek. Reuters also said Asian shares tracked Wall Street higher after a soft U.S. jobs report reduced fears of a near-term rise in borrowing costs.

items.title: S&P 500 rises, with broad risk assets supported by softer U.S. rate expectations
items.summary: Market data cited by Reuters showed the S&P 500 up 0.62%, alongside gains in the Euro STOXX 50, FTSE 100, and Nikkei 225. U.S. Treasury yields were little changed, suggesting traders are still balancing growth and inflation risks.

items.title: Oil steadies as Strait of Hormuz uncertainty eases but remains a market focus
items.summary: Reuters reported that oil prices held broadly steady after Iran said it was nearing a final pact with Oman on new shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz. The geopolitical backdrop kept energy markets in focus even as broader equities firmed.

items.title: U.S. labor market weakens, with unemployment falling to 4.1% and payrolls down
items.summary: MarketWatch said the U.S. unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, its lowest level in 13 months, while other reporting pointed to a loss of 23,000 jobs in July. The combination reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve may have less reason to tighten policy in the near term.

items.title: Fed-watch focus shifts to inflation after soft jobs report
items.summary: Reuters noted that investors were awaiting the next U.S. inflation reading after the weaker payrolls data shifted attention from labor-market resilience to price pressures. The market reaction suggested that the path for Fed policy now depends heavily on the upcoming CPI print.

items.title: BOJ rate-hike expectations complicated by domestic bond-market pressures
items.summary: Reuters highlighted that the Bank of Japan’s rate-hike path is running into market problems tied to Japanese bond yields and domestic political constraints. Japanese equities still rose, with the Nikkei 225 gaining 1.81% in Reuters’ market snapshot.

items.title: Indonesia moves toward naming a new central bank governor
items.summary: Reuters reported that Indonesia nominated Destry Damayanti as the sole candidate for central bank governor. The move is notable for emerging-market policy watchers because leadership changes can affect currency and rate expectations.

items.title: European and U.S. market sentiment improved as investors balanced growth and policy risks
items.summary: Reuters and MarketScreener both showed firming sentiment in Europe, with the Euro STOXX 50 and DAX slightly higher and investor morale in the euro zone turning positive in August. The move reflected a modest improvement in risk appetite despite ongoing data and geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway reports higher second-quarter net earnings and revenue
items.summary: MarketScreener listed Berkshire Hathaway among the day’s notable company items, saying the conglomerate’s second-quarter net earnings and revenue rose. The report would be closely watched by investors for clues on insurance performance and the breadth of Berkshire’s operating strength.

items.title: Palantir jumps after strong market attention in trading screens
items.summary: MarketScreener’s 24-hour market movers showed Palantir Technologies up 10.32%, making it one of the standout stock moves in the session. The sharp rise indicates unusually strong investor interest, though the search results do not specify a single catalyst.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin’s BIP-110 split leaves minority chain behind as main network advances
items.summary: Bitcoin’s BIP-110 soft fork attempt has split supporters onto a minority chain, while the main network has continued pulling ahead. TradingView also reported the branch stalled after two blocks, indicating limited traction for the fork effort.

items.title: Senate Clarity Act vote pushed toward September
items.summary: U.S. Senate Republican leaders have delayed the Clarity Act vote until after the August recess, setting up a potential September 15 Senate vote. The delay keeps major crypto market-structure legislation in focus for regulators and industry participants.

items.title: Brazil tightens crypto fraud controls with self-custody transfer delay
items.summary: Brazil is moving to require a 24-hour wait on some transfers to self-custody wallets as part of stronger fraud controls. A related central bank resolution also requires exchanges to delay certain crypto transfers above $10,000 to foreign platforms and self-custody wallets starting Jan. 1, 2027.

items.title: Bitcoin rises above $65,000 after weak U.S. jobs data
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed above $65,000 after a surprise miss in U.S. jobs data, which boosted risk appetite. Binance Square also reported BTC trading near $64,156, up 0.91% over 24 hours, with most major cryptocurrencies mixed.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ether ETFs post strong inflows despite muted volume
items.summary: Bitcoin and ether ETFs drew $1.1 billion in their best inflow week since April, even with low trading volume. This suggests continued institutional demand despite a broader market with mixed price action.

items.title: BTC and ETH hold gains while XRP remains weak
items.summary: Market trackers reported Bitcoin recovering above $62,000 and Ethereum holding near $1,650, while XRP stayed weak and ETF outflows continued to weigh on sentiment. InvestingNews also reported BTC around US$64,929.85, ETH at US$1,917.06, and XRP down 2% over 24 hours.

items.title: XRPL v3.3.0 proposes encrypted transfers for tokenized assets
items.summary: XRPL version 3.3.0 introduces a Confidential Transfers amendment designed to encrypt MPT balances and payment amounts. The proposal targets more than $530 million in non-RLUSD tokenized assets on the ledger.

items.title: Tether expands tokenization push into Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Tether announced plans to bring institutional-grade real estate assets onchain in Saudi Arabia as part of its real-world asset tokenization business. The move extends the company’s blockchain infrastructure efforts beyond stablecoins.

items.title: Trump Media and Crypto.com end partnership
items.summary: Trump Media and Crypto.com ended their partnership as the companies shifted priorities. The break marks a notable business development in the crypto sector’s media and exchange alliance landscape.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic updates Claude Fable 5 biology safeguards
items.summary: Anthropic said it updated Claude Fable 5’s biology safeguards to reduce false positives, cutting biology-related “fallbacks” by about 85% in testing across product surfaces. This is one of the clearest recent safety-focused model updates in the last 24 hours.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Code beta for terminal coding
items.summary: Meta launched Muse Code in beta, a terminal coding agent powered by Muse Spark 1.2. The product is priced as a coding-focused model and is aimed at software-development workflows.

items.title: Ooredoo, Nvidia, Nokia and Indosat launch Indonesia AI compute platform
items.summary: The companies launched Zankore, described as Indonesia’s first dedicated AI compute and neocloud platform. Ooredoo said it owns a 49% stake and committed $800 million to the initiative.

items.title: Firmus raises $2 billion for AI data center expansion
items.summary: Sydney-based AI data center company Firmus raised $2 billion from investors including Coatue and Nvidia, according to Reuters. The funding values the company at $10.5 billion post-money, up from $5.5 billion in April.

items.title: QuantHealth raises $45 million for AI clinical trial simulation
items.summary: QuantHealth, which provides AI software for simulating clinical trials, raised a $45 million Series B led by Qumra Capital. The round brings the company’s total funding to roughly $70 million.

items.title: US regulators review how Chinese AI firms access Nvidia chips overseas
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that the US Commerce Department’s BIS is reviewing whether Chinese AI companies are accessing Nvidia chips through legally rented foreign data centers. The move signals tighter scrutiny of global AI compute supply chains.

items.title: AI release tracker logs multiple new model and tool launches
items.summary: AI/TLDR said it tracked 10 new AI releases in the last 24 hours, including Claude Managed Agents spend caps and Claude Code cross-session messaging. The tracker also noted a day-by-day timeline of OpenAI’s accidental Hugging Face hack.

items.title: New wave of AI news centers on agents, safety, and infrastructure
items.summary: Across recent coverage, the dominant themes are more capable AI agents, stronger safety controls, and continued investment in compute and data centers. The mix of product launches, model safeguards, and funding rounds suggests the sector remains focused on both commercialization and operational risk.
